claim: Citadelle de Namur is open daily 10am-6pm from 1 April to 27 September 2026 (closed 20 May, 3-5 July, 21 September); the 3-attraction Citadel Pass (underground galleries OR Middle Ages tour + tourist train + Terra Nova visitor centre) costs €22 adult / €20 child, and the 4-attraction pass €36/€32.
quote: From 1 April to 27 September: Open Monday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm. Closed on 20 May, 3, 4 and 5 July and 21 September. Citadel Pass (3 visits) €22 / €20. Citadel Pass (4 visits) €36 / €32.

claim: Parking at the Citadelle de Namur Esplanade is free and unlimited except during events, but Route Merveilleuse between Terra Nova and the Esplanade is closed for works until end of March 2026.
quote: Parking at the Esplanade is free and available permanently except during certain events ... Route Merveilleuse is inaccessible between Terra Nova and the Esplanade until the end of March 2026.

claim: The Terra Nova Visitor Centre, housed in the former 1820-1825 Dutch barracks on the Citadelle de Namur site, presents 2000 years of Namur and European military history via a floating wall of screens, a plan-relief scale model and audio guides in six languages, and is accessible to people with reduced mobility.
quote: In the old Terra Nova barracks, visitors walk along a floating wall of screens and images that narrate the story of life in Namur from the dawn of time to the present day ... 2000 years of European urban and military history ... Audio guides are available in French, Dutch, English, German, Spanish and Chinese.

claim: Citadelle de Dinant is open daily 10am-6pm April-September and 10am-4:30pm October-March; standard ticket including HistoPad augmented-reality guide is €15 adult / €13 child (4-12), with a 3-in-1 package adding a 45-minute Meuse cruise at €25 adult / €20 child; recommended self-guided visit is ~1h30.
quote: April to September: Daily 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM. October to March: Daily 10:00 AM – 4:30 PM. Standard Visit (includes HistoPad): Adult €15.00, Child (ages 4-12) €13.00. 3-in-1 Package (Citadel + HistoPad + 45-minute cruise): €25.00/adult, €20.00/child. Around 1 hour 30 minutes.

claim: Two free car/coach parking areas, EV charging points and a bike rack are available at the top of the Citadelle de Dinant, but the cable car is closed for major renovation, so visitors arrive by car at the summit or climb the 408-step staircase from the town centre.
quote: Two complimentary parking areas for cars and coaches. Bike rack at the top of the site. Electric vehicle charging points available ... A historic 408-step staircase connects Dinant town centre directly to the fortress.

claim: Château de Vêves at Celles (Houyet) is open Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays 10am-5pm from 30 March to 1 November 2026, daily during Flemish Easter holidays (6-19 April), daily 6 July-23 August, and daily during All Saints holidays 19 October-1 November; last admission 4:30pm.
quote: From 30 March to 01 November 2026 The Castle is open on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm ... From 6 July to 23 August 2026 The Castle is open every day (Monday to Sunday) from 10:00 to 17:00 ... The Castle closes at 5:00 pm (last admission at 4:30 pm).

claim: Château de Vêves admission is €9.50 adult, €8.50 senior/student/teacher, €6.50 child (under 4 free); group rate (20+) €8 adult / €6 child; optional treasure hunt +€2.75, and children are dressed as knights and princesses free of charge during the visit.
quote: Adults: €9.50 - Seniors (60+), students, teachers: €8.50 - Children: €6.50 - Children under 4: Free. Treasure hunt option: +€2.75 per person. All children are dressed free as knights and princesses during their visit.

claim: Château de Freÿr near Hastière is open Thursday-Sunday and public holidays 11am-5pm from 4 April to 15 November 2026, with extended Tuesday-Sunday opening 1 July-31 August; admission €12 adult, €10 senior/student/adolescent, free for children under 12 with adult; on-site parking for cars, coaches and bikes; last entry 45 minutes before closing.
quote: April 4 – November 15: Thursday–Sunday & public holidays, 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. July 1 – August 31: Tuesday–Sunday & public holidays, 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Adult €12, Senior/Adolescent/Student €10, Children (up to 12 years, with adult) Free. Parking for coach buses, cars, bikes.

claim: Freÿr is a 16th-17th century Renaissance château on the Meuse facing the Freÿr cliffs whose 30,000 m² French-style gardens hold 9 ponds, 33 orange trees still in their 18th-century crates, hornbeam labyrinth hedges and a Moretti-decorated pavilion — classed as Wallonia's protected heritage.
quote: Freÿr is a Renaissance castle ... The French-style gardens feature flowerbeds and arbours, ponds, fountains and orange trees set against the impressive backdrop of the Meuse and its cliffs. The gardens comprise 30,000 m² of hedges, 9 ponds, 33 orange trees and a pavilion decorated by the Moretti brothers.

claim: Château de Lavaux-Sainte-Anne (near Rochefort, ~40km from Profondeville so just outside the 30km radius) opens Wed-Sun 10am-6pm (daily in school holidays), last entry 4:45pm; €9.50 adult / €8.50 senior-student / €6 child (3-12, costume included); free on-site parking; 1-3h visit covering 32 furnished rooms across three museums (Lords of Lavaux, rural Famenne, nature/hunting) plus French gardens and a wetland reserve.
quote: Opens Wednesday-Sunday, 10 am–6 pm year-round (last entry 4:45 pm) ... Adult: €9.50, Senior (65+)/Student: €8.50, Child (3–12): €6 (includes costume rental). Free parking available on-site. Between 1 and 3 hours. 32 furnished and decorated rooms across three museums.

claim: Château de Spontin in Yvoir (in the Bocq valley ~12km east of Profondeville) opens Tue-Sun 10am-5pm in July-August, Wed/Sat/Sun 2pm-5pm in September-October, and daily 2pm-5pm (except Mon) from 28 April during spring break; €8 adult, €5 child under 12, guided group €7pp — but private events may close it unexpectedly so call ahead.
quote: July & August: Tuesday-Sunday, 10am-5pm. September & October: Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday, 2pm-5pm. Spring break (from April 28): Daily 2pm-5pm except Mondays. Adults: €8, Children (under 12): €5. Certain weekends or opening days may be exceptionally closed to the public.

claim: The 13th-century feudal Château de Spontin is one of the rare castles in Belgium to preserve a still-functioning authentic drawbridge, was reopened to visitors after years of closure following its purchase by a private owner, and sits beside the scenic Bocq tourist railway in the valley.
quote: Le château féodal de Spontin ... est l'un des rares châteaux de Belgique à avoir conservé un authentique pont-levis en état de fonctionnement.

claim: Château de Lavaux-Sainte-Anne is about 29 km by road from Dinant (which itself is 15 km from Profondeville), making the total drive from Arbre/Profondeville roughly 40-45 km — just outside the strict 30 km radius but still a feasible day-trip add-on.
quote: The distance between Dinant and Château de Lavaux-Sainte-Anne is 13 miles (approximately 21 kilometers), with a road distance of 17.8 miles (approximately 29 kilometers). It takes approximately 21 minutes to drive.

claim: Profondeville sits ~12-15 km south of Namur and ~15 km north of Dinant on the N92 along the Meuse, placing Citadelle de Namur, Citadelle de Dinant, Château de Freÿr (~22 km), Château de Spontin (~12 km), Château de Vêves at Celles (~20-25 km) all within the 30 km radius; Bouillon at ~66-88 km is well outside.
quote: Profondeville et Namur ... 12.5 km ... 17 minutes ... La distance en ligne droite entre Bouillon et Profondeville est 65.10 km, mais la distance à parcourir en voiture est de 88 km.
